column4: Visit note | 2026-01-08 03:30 PM | Dr. Arif Hossain, Pulmonology | Patient: Riad Mondal, 56, male. Mr. Mondal attends for a follow-up review of his chronic breathing issues, noting that he has been coughing at night, experiencing a tight chest when exposed to dust or cold air, and hearing a noticeable wheeze. He mentions that his symptoms flared during the winter smog in Rampura. He works as a bank officer, sits for long hours, and continues to manage his daily routine despite the discomfort. He denies fever, chest pain, or recent weight loss. On examination: SpO2 92%, BP 113/79 mmHg, pulse 87 bpm, weight 97 kg. Auscultation reveals bilateral expiratory wheezes; no crackles are heard. Assessment: Bronchial asthma. Plan: chronic follow-up: continue current medicines, no new prescription issued. No new medicine was prescribed today. He was advised to avoid dust and smoke, keep the bedroom well aired, and learn the correct inhaler technique. Follow-up in 1 month to check inhaler technique.
